cases.note: Each session edits every fourth byte of the same file at once, one pwrite per byte. A store that cannot write in place answers a pwrite by reading the file and writing it back whole, so without one writer at a time per path a session put back bytes another had just replaced.

program.python:
import os
fd = os.open('/data/f.txt', os.O_WRONLY)
for offset in range(0, 20, 4):
    os.pwrite(fd, b'A', offset)
os.close(fd)

import os
fd = os.open('/data/f.txt', os.O_WRONLY)
for offset in range(1, 20, 4):
    os.pwrite(fd, b'B', offset)
os.close(fd)

import os
fd = os.open('/data/f.txt', os.O_WRONLY)
for offset in range(2, 20, 4):
    os.pwrite(fd, b'C', offset)
os.close(fd)

import os
fd = os.open('/data/f.txt', os.O_WRONLY)
for offset in range(3, 20, 4):
    os.pwrite(fd, b'D', offset)
os.close(fd)

cases.note: Each session appends a line to the same file at once; every line lands, in some order.
